recommendation: Keep this source fix as-is. Do not revert the current slice() prose to the exact 2023 Jira resolution wording because later accepted FHIR-45455 refinement clarifies the parameter semantics; future slice() edge-case behavior should be handled by a new tracker.
issue_request: FHIR-42983 was an Applied/Persuasive with Modification FHIR-core FHIR-I clarification for FHIRPath.slice. It asked the FHIRPath page to clarify that slice() filters the current collection to elements matching a named slice, document %profile for profile constraints, address slice-name context, explain why the profile argument is required, include an example, and warn that not all FHIRPath engines can implement slice().
initial_application: Commit 450527a6bd initially applied the Jira resolution to source/fhirpath.html. Commit f3149e9502 later refined the same slice()/%profile section while applying related FHIR-45455 and FHIR-42983, adding %profile to the FHIR-specific variables list, documenting structure/name argument semantics, and adding the current example and implementation note.
additional_context: FHIR-I minutes from 2023-10-23 confirm the 9-0-0 persuasive-with-modification vote. The later #fhir/infrastructure-wg Zulip thread on the fhirpath slice() definition confirms the intended direction: slice() filters input elements, %profile belongs in the variables section, and unresolved edge cases should not block the applied clarification. FHIR-45455 is the same change family and already has a combined-branch reconcile audit, so it was not republished here.
reconciliation: The substantive slice() text was already correct, but the variables-section lead-in still said FHIR defines two variables while listing %resource, %rootResource, and %profile. This commit changes that lead-in to three variables and leaves the later accepted slice() parameter prose intact.
source_changes: source/fhirpath.html: changed the FHIR-specific variables lead-in from "two specific variables" to "three specific variables" to match %resource, %rootResource, and %profile.
